Three.js downloaded. Now design a full 3D game.

Architecture:
- `index.html`: new UI with language selector (flag/globe, select with many languages), auth card, HUD, dialogue box (Steve/Mirza), game over, pause, controls, sound/music toggles, dialogue toggle.
- `game.js` (module) — imports THREE from './vendor/three.module.js'.
- i18n dictionary for UI + dialogue lines for ~12-16 languages. "toute les langues" impossible literally, but we can support a wide range of languages and a language picker with 20 languages. We should be honest in final note: 20 languages supported incl. RTL Arabic, with UI localization and dialogue translations. Could add more but reasonable.

Dialogue: Steve and Mirza banter during the run. Each dialogue has:
- spokenFrench: actual French sentence
- translations: {fr, en, es, de, it, pt, ar, zh, ja, ko, ru, hi, nl, tr, pl, sv, id, uk, ...}
- Use speechSynthesis to speak the French line (with fr-FR voice), toggled by a "Voix" button. Subtitles display in the selected language, plus the French original in small text. This satisfies "peuvent parfois parler pour de vrai en langue française et traduite soit en français ou anglais ou autre langue".

Need real voices that sound different for Steve and Mirza: use pitch/rate differences, pick French voices (male/female if available). SpeechSynthesis requires user gesture on some browsers; primary CTA (start game) is a gesture, good. We'll add voice toggle and ensure.

Dialogue mode: maybe automatic banter every ~12s during run, with a speech bubble UI at bottom-left. Also a "Dialogue" button opens a chat panel where you can trigger banter? The request says "le mode dialogue entre Steve et Mirza" — a dialogue mode. We can implement a toggle "Mode dialogue" that enables mid-run dialogue + speech. Default on. The dialogue box shows portrait avatars (SVG/canvas?), name, translated subtitle, small FR line, and translation language badge. Auto-advance.

3D game:
- Three.js scene: sky gradient (large sphere or background color + fog), directional sun light, hemisphere light.
- Snowy terrain: long plane with slope? Infinite runner with camera following. Use repeating segments to create downhill track with curve? Simpler: rider fixed around z=0 moving forward in -z; world objects move toward camera. Camera behind and above. Track width ~ 3 lanes (x = -2.6, 0, 2.6). Terrain large plane with snow material, slight downhill via rotation? Could make track flat but visually downhill with mountains. Better: track is a long ribbon with a gentle slope; camera follows rider. Creating a curved slope complicates collision. Use flat plane but fog and mountain backdrop for depth. Add side walls of snow banks and trees.

Gameplay: rider auto-moves; obstacles spawn far in -z and move toward rider (+z) at speed. Lane switch left/right, jump (with gravity, y). Coins rotate and collect. Speed ramps. Score = distance.

Rider model: snowboard (rounded box) + body (capsule/cylinder), head sphere with beanie + goggles, arms/legs using cylinders. Lean into turns. Add particle snow spray behind board when turning, plus motion streaks. Use instanced meshes? Simple.

Environment:
- Terrain: PlaneGeometry large, MeshStandardMaterial white with slight blue; add subtle bumps via vertex displacement? Keep simple.
- Track: a slightly darker groomed strip (planes with stripes) — maybe not.
- Trees: cone layers + trunk, scattered on both sides, recycled as they pass.
- Rocks: dodecahedron geometry, dark gray with snow cap (smaller white dodecahedron).
- Gates: two poles with banner — the "gate" obstacle maybe a red slalom gate you must dodge? Current game had gate obstacles. In 3D, use red/blue slalom flags/poles as obstacles? Better obstacles: rocks and logs. Keep gates as decorative slalom gates that don't kill? To match gameplay: obstacles = rocks; gates = jumpable barrier bars? Let's use "rocks" and "gates" (small barrier with a gap?). Simpler: obstacles are gray rocks and red "barrières". Jump over both; collision if not jumping.
- Coins: gold torus rings, rotating, collect on proximity.
- Mountains: cone/pyramid meshes with snow, placed far; background gradient via scene.background color + fog and a large sky dome shader.

Camera: position (0, 5.2, 8.5) relative to rider, looking at rider + forward. Slight dynamic FOV with speed. Smooth lane follow via lerp.

Performance: keep under ~120 objects, pixelRatio clamp 2.

Input: swipe on mobile (left/right/up), buttons, keyboard arrows/A/D/W/Space. Add pointer swipe detection on canvas.

UI design: keep snow aesthetic but more premium. Use language selector top-right. Auth card with big title, tabs, fields, best score. After login, show HUD: distance, coins, speed, dialogue voice toggle, pause. Dialogue box at bottom center-left above controls with Steve/Mirza avatar (colored circles with initials or emoji), name, subtitle in selected language and French original small.

Language: define `LANGS` object with codes and labels. UI strings: login, signup, username, password, enter, create, errors, best, coins, speed, pause, resume, quit, retry, logout, gameOver, distance, dialogue, voiceOn, voiceOff, translating, etc. For "all languages", support e.g. 24 languages: fr, en, es, de, it, pt, nl, pl, sv, no, da, fi, tr, ru, uk, ar, he, hi, bn, zh, ja, ko, id, vi, th, el, ro, cs, hu. That's a lot of translation work. We can include ~16 major ones fully and fallback to French/English for others? Fallback would be dishonest. Let's do a solid set of 18 languages with UI strings and dialogue translations. Hmm token budget but doable.

To reduce translation volume, dialogue lines could have translations generated for 8 languages and the UI for 18. But the user says dialogue translated into French or English or another language. So dialogue translation for several languages suffices; separate from full UI support. Let's do UI for 15 languages and dialogue for fr, en, es, de, it, pt, ar, zh, ja, ko, ru, hi, tr, nl. That's 14, decent. For languages without a dialogue translation, fall back to English and show "EN" badge.

Maybe better: 12 UI languages: FR, EN, ES, DE, IT, PT, AR, ZH, JA, KO, RU, HI, TR, NL, PL = 15. Plus language selector "Autre" not needed.

Let me make translation tables carefully with correct text.

Dialogue content (Steve & Mirza, snowboard buddies): ~14 exchanges with French spoken line and translations. Keep lines short and fun, some friendly banter. Include some French slang. Audio via speechSynthesis.

Examples:
1. Steve: "Allez Mirza, on descend ! La montagne n'attend pas." — EN "Come on Mirza, let's go! The mountain won't wait."
2. Mirza: "Steve, tu as encore oublié de serrer tes fixations ?" — EN "Steve, did you forget to tighten your bindings again?"
3. Steve: "Regarde ces pièces ! On dirait que la piste est en or aujourd'hui."
4. Mirza: "Saute au bon moment, sinon tu vas manger la neige."
5. Steve: "La neige est parfaite. Même les pingouins seraient jaloux."
6. Mirza: "Concentre-toi, il y a un rocher devant toi !"
7. Steve: "Je suis né sur cette planche, Mirza."
8. Mirza: "Né sur une planche ? Tu es surtout né pour tomber."
9. Steve: "Écoute ce silence... juste le vent et nous."
10. Mirza: "Et moi qui croyais que tu parlais seulement aux sapins."
11. Steve: "On est les rois de la pente !"
12. Mirza: "Les rois de la pente qui oublient de freiner..."
13. Steve: "Un jour, on descendra cette montagne jusqu'à la mer."
14. Mirza: "D'accord, mais d'abord, évite ce rocher !"
15. Steve: "Tu entends ça ? La montagne nous répond."
16. Mirza: "C'est ton estomac, Steve."

"vous avez le language de toute les langues" — implement language switch that instantly retranslates UI, dialogue subtitles, toasts, hints.

Now 3D implementation details.

Three.js module import. Since `--directory public` and module script works with same-origin. Use `<script type="module" src="game.js"></script>`.

Scene setup:
```js
const scene = new THREE.Scene();
scene.fog = new THREE.Fog(0xcfe9f2, 35, 120);
```
Sky: big sphere with ShaderMaterial gradient, BackSide.

Renderer: antialias, shadowMap PCFSoft, toneMapping ACESFilmic, outputColorSpace SRGB. Pixel ratio min(devicePixelRatio, 2). Set clear color.

Lighting: HemisphereLight(0xbfe3ff, 0x67808f, 1.1); DirectionalLight(0xfff3dd, 2.2) with shadows camera ortho covering around rider; its target follows.

Ground: PlaneGeometry(200, 260, 40, 40), rotate -PI/2, position z=-80. Vertex displacement small sine noise for snow bumps? Use MeshStandardMaterial({color:0xf5fbff, roughness:0.95}). Add lane grooves: thin dark-ish translucent planes running along z (3 lanes edges) — long BoxGeometry(0.06, 0.01, 250) lightly blue. Also add sparse snow sparkle points? Maybe skip.

Track side banks: two long white mounds using cylinders rotated along z? Could use long boxes with rounded shape — simpler: series of snowbanks (scaled spheres) recycled? Use 2 big CapsuleGeometry? Capsule along z is possible by rotating. Add Mesh with radius 2, length 220, rotate X PI/2, positioned x=±9, y=0.8 — gives snow banks. Color white. These will look nice.

Mountains: create 10-14 cones at z=-90..-160, x=-80..80, heights 25-55, white with rocky base? Use ConeGeometry(radius, height, 6-8) plus snow material, and maybe second cone with slightly different color. Add distant peaks, fog blends.

Trees: build prototype tree group (trunk cylinder + 3 cones in dark green + snow caps smaller cones). Clone 40-60 across sides. Move toward +z each frame by speed; wrap z when > 20 back to -140. Trees at |x| between 8 and 26.

Obstacles: pooled arrays. Each spawn: type rock/log/barrier/coin, lane index, z = -110 to -130. Move by speed*dt to +z. Collision when z > -1.5 and < 1.5? Rider at z=0. For coins: distance in x < 1.1 and z within [-1.8,1.8] and y close (coins at y=1.2, rider y=jumpY+0.6) — collect regardless of jump? Coins elevated; allow if jumpY near. Keep simple: collect when lateral and z overlap, regardless of y (generous). Obstacles: collide if |x - riderX| < 1.15 and z in [-1.3,1.5] and jumpY < 1.0. Barrier height 1.4, rock 1.2. Jump apex ~2.2, so above threshold.
